name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PlayActorVoiceSeB
summary: Variant of 0x003CC250: plays the widget's own SE id from record+0xBA, then the same 3D-mode redirect and 0x158/0x15D voice fallback.
evidence: Same 0x4244 redirect and 0x158/0x15D ladder as 0x003CC250 with the extra record+0xBA SE; damaged Thumb body, no caller.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_PlaySe50WhenThrottled
summary: Timed part update: forwards to a child vtable slot and, while the latch at +0x1C4 is set and the predicate 0x00649BFC holds with the timer above 10.0f (0x41200000), lazily creates the shared sound player, plays SE 50 once and clears the latch.

name: Sound_PlayCommonSe300
summary: Plays the shared 'common' SE 300 through the sound player singleton. Ten named callers (battle action sequences, actor update, talk window, field party) show it is a global one-shot SE helper, so the previous 'FieldParty_' scope was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_CommitScene
summary: Scene-flow commit: when the pending transition has finished and Ui_SceneFlow_AllTransitionsDone holds, it initialises the scene sprite set (f_B4) and scene (f_5C), binds all event natives (f_6C), loads world-map models and bumps the flow counter f_1D. Body is damaged (unaff_r4/r5, in_s16).
evidence: Named callees Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_Init, Gfx_Scene_Init, Event_Script_BindAllNatives, Ui_SceneFlow_LoadWorldMapModels and Ui_SceneFlow_AllTransitionsDone all belong to one path, but the arguments are lost to damaged decompilation.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Reset
summary: Short reset: clears +0xF2, clears the slot word at +0x53 unless the battle byte (battleWork+0x4248) is 1, calls virtual +0x20 and clears f_3F. Called from Gfx_Scene_Init.
evidence: Body fully visible and the only caller is the named Gfx_Scene_Init (0x00206BBC), but the owning class is a generic widget (undeclared arg4 in Ghidra).

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DispatchByRowCount
summary: Step installed by Ui_StreetPassVipMsg_Ctor: ticks the widget; on confirm it counts the named rows of the work data panel (work+0x24A98), counts the roster entries and marks how many are named, compares them and dispatches one of five follow-up handlers through the table at 0x007291F0, storing the next handler in self+0x11C/+0x120.
evidence: Named callees Work_CountNamedRows, Spirit_CountRosterEntries, Work_AreAllDataPanelRowsUsed and maybe_Work_RowIdIsNamed plus the single caller Ui_StreetPassVipMsg_Ctor; the five-way dispatch is visible but the handler meanings are not.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateEx
summary: Secondary per-frame tactics-window update: ticks the widget pair; when event flag 4 is clear and the prompt is not yet confirmed it advances the command queue, pushes the pane from g_uiSakusenWindowPaneCallbacks, enables the input subsystem and plays a sound; otherwise it only locates the fixed command entry.
evidence: Named callees Ui_SakusenWindow_PushPane, Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt, Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry and Ui_PromptRef_IsFirstChoiceConfirmed with the 0x0072A600 static block; no caller and the descriptor block is not proven to be the tactics window's.

name: Ui_UpdateWindowOpen
signature: void Ui_UpdateWindowOpen(UiWindow* uiWindow, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Vtable slot 0x00729A24 of a window: ticks the child widget and advances the command queue, then pushes pane animation 99 (prompt confirmed, state byte 4) or 100 (state byte 5) using g_uiCampMenuPaneDescriptor values.
evidence: Body fully visible: Ui_Widget_Update, Ui_CommandQueue_Advance, Ui_PromptRef_IsFirstChoiceConfirmed, func_002BBAD0(99/100) and Ui_CampMenu_PushPane, with the state byte written as 4 or 5 - matching an 'open window' animation step.

name: maybe_Actor_ActionSeq_FinishDataPanel
summary: End step of the party-data-panel action sequence: ticks the widget at sequence+0x34D8; on confirm it compares the remaining node count (owner+0x34/+0x38, 16-byte stride) plus the roster count with 0x33 and requests step 0x0F when below, 5 otherwise; on cancel it requests step 3.
evidence: Named callees Ui_Widget_Update, Ui_PromptRef_IsFirstChoiceConfirmed, Spirit_CountRosterEntries and Game_GetWork, and the same +0x34D8/+0x3574 layout as 0x00308B9C; the '0x33 threshold' meaning (max rows) is inferred.

name: Ui_Object_NotifyOverlayManager
summary: UI object step: ticks the widget pair (object+0xCC0 / +0x120) and, when it finishes, notifies the UI overlay manager ((work+8)+0x48) through 0x0023CDC4 and requests step 0x0D by setting the step controller's +? fields.
evidence: FACTS verify (work+8)+0x48 is the UI overlay manager, and the body passes exactly that pointer to 0x0023CDC4 before writing step 0x0D; the called notification itself is still unnamed.

name: Ui_Window_SyncRecordAndAdvance
summary: Window step gated by Ui_Menu_UpdateModeTransition and a widget-idle check plus a timer above 0x3FFFFFFF: copies the work record at work+0x2E2F8 into self+0x984, mirrors its +0x1808 flag, and requests step 4 then commits.
evidence: All three gates and the record copy (func_002A48C8, work+0x2E2F8, +0x1808 mirror) are visible in the body and named; the only assumption left is that the record copy is a 'sync'.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdatePaneCommand
summary: Per-frame tactics-window handler: ticks the message widget pair and, when idle, queues a fixed command entry via Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry with the first two words of g_uiSakusenWindowPaneDescriptors. The literal pair is aliased in the decompilation, so the specific entry is unknown.
evidence: Body is 60 bytes: Ui_Widget_Update + Func_0062F680 gate + Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry against g_uiSakusenWindowPaneDescriptors; no caller, and the aliased constants hide which entry is queued.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdatePaneCommandB
summary: Template copy of 0x002A2820: ticks the message widget pair and queues a fixed command entry when idle, using the descriptor block at 0x0072A610 instead of 0x0072A600.
evidence: Byte-identical body to 0x002A2820 apart from the descriptor literal; no caller distinguishes the two.

name: maybe_Item_BuildCandidateList_ByCategoryRange
summary: Item-candidate builder restricted to the equipment id ranges (id-0xA4 < 0x91B or id-0xB19 < 4) whose ItemRecord+0x29 equals the category argument, with the usual 0x20/0x40 flag gate and sorted insertion into list+0x0A.
evidence: The range test and the +0x29 category compare match the FACTS equipment ranges exactly (0xA4..0x9BF and 0xB19..0xB1C), and the walk is bounded by 0x91B+0x220; no caller names the owning menu.

name: maybe_Item_BuildCandidateList_OneOrTwoHanded
summary: Item-candidate builder whose acceptance test is the OR of the one-handed (func_0066C5A8) and two-handed (func_0066C5CC) equip-category predicates after the 0x20/0x40 flag gate, inserting the surviving equip ids sorted.
evidence: FACTS identify 0x0066C5A8 (1H categories 0..4) and 0x0066C5CC (2H 5..9), so the old 'TwoFilters' label can be replaced by what the two predicates actually are.

name: maybe_Item_AssignEquipSlotItem
signature: void maybe_Item_AssignEquipSlotItem(void* equipChoice, int slotIndex, u32 itemId)
summary: Writes itemId into the equip-slot word at self+0x0E+slotIndex*2 and, when the new or the currently equipped item is one- or two-handed, compares their equip categories (+0x29) and may clear the stored item (f_10=0xFFFF) to avoid an illegal combination.
evidence: Body uses Item_LookupRecord, func_0066C5A8/func_0066C5CC (1H/2H per FACTS) and ItemRecord+0x29; the single caller symbol (Effect_UpdateBillboardOrientation) contradicts the body and is almost certainly a mis-resolved neighbour.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePartB
signature: void* maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePartB(void* self, u32 recordHandle, u32 flag)
summary: Installs g_uiCompositeStatusVtable, creates the embedded sub-object, allocates and constructs a 0x4AC-byte DiveStartWindow part, registers it via Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, applies the record handle and marks the part active (+0x94=1) before running its update slot.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePart
signature: unsigned int maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_CreatePart(unsigned int partId, unsigned int forwarded, unsigned int forwarded2, unsigned int forwarded3)
summary: Thumb part factory: byte-swaps the part id, constructs it with Ui_DiveStartWindowPart_Ctor, registers it through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, stores it at +8, applies the record handle, marks the part controller active (+0x94=1) and runs its update slot. Twin of the ARM copy 0x002959F4.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState
summary: Per-frame status-window update: bails while busy, waits on the transition object at self[2], and in state 3 rebuilds the party summary bytes at GameWork+0x2E2F4/+0x2E2F5 (active slot count and a clamped count value) before switching to state 0x3D.
evidence: Named callees Ui_StatusWindow_CountActiveSlots, Party_GetSecondRowNameLength, Work_AreAllNamedRowsUsed and Ui_Window_SetState support the status-window reading; the only caller is the DiveStartWindow part builder, so the owner stays inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_StepBranchOnFlag8
summary: Message-window control step: releases the root, tests progress flag bit 8 and pushes tag bytes 0x22..0x25 (flag clear, then set it) or 0x21/0x20 (flag set) into the control string at +0x1944, then pops the next control code and executes it. The tag bytes' meaning is an interpretation.
evidence: Named callees Message_TestFlagMask(...,8), Ui_Root_SetFlagBits, Ui_Root_ReleaseAll, Ui_MessageWindow_ExecControlCode and std_String_PushBackByte; callers are credit-window and list-screen steps, so the 'message window' owner is inherited rather than proven.

name: maybe_Script_Object_ReleaseTemporaries
signature: void maybe_Script_Object_ReleaseTemporaries(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, int* loop, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, int* refcounted)
summary: Squirrel-style refcount cleanup: walks a 0x14-byte record array and, for every temporary whose tag has the 0x8000000 bit set, decrements the refcount and calls the virtual +8 release when it reaches zero. The old 'ThumbStub' name said nothing about this.
evidence: The repeated (word & 0x8000000) / refcount-- / virtual +8 pattern is visible four times in the surviving body; the function is ARM (not Thumb) and the decompilation has bad instruction data, so the record layout stays unknown.

name: maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure
signature: void maybe_Script_VM_RunClosure(unsigned int vm, unsigned int closure, void* fn, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Large Squirrel VM helper (5 KB, only the entry block recovered): reads the closure reference with the 0x50415254 marker through Script_ReadClosureRef, then a serialized value, and dispatches into Script_CallAllArgs; 'RunClosure' remains a description of the visible prologue only.
evidence: Named callees Script_ReadClosureRef (0x001651CC), Script_ReadSerializedValue, Script_ObjectPtr_Assign, Script_CallAllArgs and caller Script_RegisterHook confirm VM code, but most of the body is truncated with halt_baddata.

name: maybe_Save_LoadSlotRecords

summary: Save/archive loader: narrow-to-wide name conversion, Fs_SplitResourceName, Fs_ArchiveEntry_ReadInto into a 0xC8B0-byte payload, then the Save_LoadSlotHeader / Save_LoadSlotData / Save_BuildSlotFilePaths chain to fill the save work. Prologue is damaged.

name: maybe_Item_TransferSourceToBag
summary: Moves item ids from a source record into the player's bag one entry at a time (up to a requested count, stopping when the data panel is full): reads the id at source+0x734, and for ids in 0xAA3..0xB3A adds them via 0x00613168 and Item_Set_InsertItemId, then requests follow-up step 0x23 or 0x24. The old 'CollectIdsFromBag' name described the opposite direction.
evidence: Recovered body shows the source-record loop, Item_LookupRecord per entry, the 0xAA3..0xB3A range (same range as 0x005D9C84/0x00283488), Work_AreAllDataPanelRowsUsed as the stop condition, and the vtable +0x54 step requests 0x23/0x24.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_AdvancePage5
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ListWindow_AdvancePage5(u32 window, int seqDesc, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: List-window page step: ticks the page widget; on page 9 confirm (or page 10 cancel) it sets the list counts, builds mode-5 entries and requests action 0x0C, otherwise it refreshes the save work and requests 0x10/0x11 depending on func_00383A80(root).
evidence: Page ids 9/10, Ui_ListData_BuildEntries(...,5,...) and the 0x0C/0x10/0x11 step requests are literal; no caller identifies the window.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_OpenPage4

evidence: Named callees Ui_ChoiceWindow_ResetOptions, Ui_ListData_BuildEntries(...,4,...) and Party_GetSecondRowNameLength; no caller, so the page number is the only anchor.

name: Party_SumSkillCostScaled
summary: Sums the per-skill byte at SkillRecord+6 over the character's learned skills that the given panel slot can unlock, and multiplies the total by 20 (display units). Raw twin of the *1 sum in 0x003AAB38.
evidence: Three named callers (Ui_SkillPanel_OnCursorMove, Ui_SkillPanel_HandleInput, Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand) plus the raw twin 0x003AAB38 prove the raw/scaled pair and the skill-panel context; only the exact meaning of the summed byte stays open.

name: Party_SumSkillCost
summary: Same sum as 0x003AA448 without the x20 scaling: adds SkillRecord+6 over every learned skill of the character that SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill accepts for the given slot and returns the raw total.
evidence: Body is identical to 0x003AA448 apart from the missing *0x14, and its callers are the skill-panel/plate-window text updates.

name: maybe_Ui_SkillList_CollectPruned
signature: void maybe_Ui_SkillList_CollectPruned(UiSkillList* self, int characterId, int slot)
summary: Builds the character's usable skill list: copies the member's 60-entry u16 skill table (0x78 bytes from +0x58/+0x5A), blanks entries the slot cannot use and repeatedly drops skills whose prerequisites are missing, compacting the survivors into the list at self+0x0E with the count at +0x8A.
evidence: Named callers Ui_SkillPanel_OnCursorMove, Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand, Ui_SixRowCountList_Refresh, Ui_PlateWindow_UpdateText and callee SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill; the 60-entry copy and the compaction loop are visible in the first 60 lines.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateUnitsForSubMode2
summary: When the action sequence is in sub-mode 2 (self[0x498]+0x1F8 == 2) with sub-state 1..3, iterates every battle unit through vtable +0x10C and dispatches the per-unit update 0x001FD10C on each.
evidence: Gate values (2 and 1..3), the unit-count helper func_00630D64, the per-unit dispatch, and six named battle-sequence callers (Battle_ActionSequence_Update_2, Battle_Sequence_Update, member-screen updates, ...).

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentDetail_ScrollNameA
summary: One direction of the equipment detail's member-name scroll: when the member's name cursor is 0 it opens the wrapped detail page, otherwise it measures the name with Item_RollStatBoostDelta, advances the cursor by that delta, formats the name fragment into arg buffer +0x848 and pushes the item detail page, then closes at the end.
evidence: Named callees Ui_Window_PushPane, Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush, Item_LookupRecord, Item_RollStatBoostDelta and Ui_ItemUse_ConsumeSourceItem prove an equipment window; which vtable slot/direction this is remains open.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentDetail_ScrollNameB
summary: Opposite name-scroll direction: clamps the member cursor into [0, max] (with f_12 as the remaining limit), sends the consumed delta as page command 10 and pushes command 0x32 only when the current item id is in the equipment ranges (0xA4..0x9BF or 0xB19..0xB1C).
evidence: Same named callee set as 0x003D6480 plus the explicit equipment id-range test from FACTS and the delta clamp logic; the direction is still inferred from the pair.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_OpenDetailForCurrentId
summary: Shared epilogue of the equipment-detail handlers: refreshes the UI, asks the panel for its current 16-bit item id via func_002BCD14 and either stores the panel reference at owner+0x10CC and pushes the detail page, or tears the panel down through 0x0019AD70 when the id is 0.
evidence: Body is Thumb-damaged (coprocessor_store, unaff_r4) and the receiver is lost, so the only support is the identical close path shared with 0x003D6480/0x003D6750.

name: Casino_Poker_DealHandE
summary: Poker deal variant: three fixed deck-slot exchanges, a second deck-4 shuffle, seven random page exchanges and a final rank-chance roll that decides whether the last slot is swapped with a random hand position, ending with the shared hand rotation.
evidence: Named helpers Casino_Poker_ShuffleDeck13/Deck4, func_00416638 (slot exchange), Casino_Poker_RollHandRankChance and Casino_Poker_RotateHandSlots, and the single caller Casino_Poker_DealAndEvaluate; only the variant letter is a disambiguator.

name: maybe_Gfx_MoveNode_CreateB
signature: void maybe_Gfx_MoveNode_CreateB(u8 mode, u32 startX, u32 startY, u32 duration)
summary: Allocates a 0xA0-byte interpolator node, constructs it with Container_NameHash_Ctor and the local dtor 0x0046B4C0, stores mode and the three start/duration words, and inserts it into the named-object map at (work+8)+0x78.
evidence: Tail is Container_NameHash_Ctor/Container_NamedMap_Insert on (work+8)+0x78 and the slot stores are visible; the callers (AddItemInPlayer, Battle_MpHealPopup_Dtor, Camera_RegularShake_Update) show the node is a generic timed tween, not a camera-only object.

name: maybe_Ui_MemberRow_BuildStatsText
summary: Builds the 0x3C0-byte stats text block for one party member row: resolves the member record from row->f_768, runs Party_StatCalc_InitContext / SetupMemberContext / ApplyBaseStats with the row's +B105/+B106 selection bytes, copies the block out and resets message arg slot 8.
evidence: The whole Party_StatCalc chain plus std_memcpy of 0x3C0 bytes and Message_FormatArgSlot_ResetC(8,...) is visible; nothing in the body is scroll-bar specific, so the old 'Ui_ScrollBar_LayoutRowLabel' prefix was unsupported.

name: maybe_Regex_State_BuildRecursive
signature: u32 maybe_Regex_State_BuildRecursive(RegexMatcher* matcher, RegexState** slot, u32 key_list, u32* key)
summary: Recursive builder for a regex sub-expression: allocates the key bitset, marks the state's own class, deduplicates and splits overlapping classes, collects child edges and recurses. Body is badly damaged (bad instruction data, dozens of removed blocks).
evidence: Caller Regex_Match_Build and callees Regex_State_FindOrCreate / Regex_ParsePredefinedClass / Regex_State_CollectEdges (neighbours) fix the subsystem; the recursion and the class-splitting helpers are named, but unaff_r4 still hides the output object.

name: Sound_MixerThread_MainThumb
signature: void Sound_MixerThread_MainThumb(u32 thread, u32 thread2, int thread3, u32 thread4, int frame)
summary: Thumb twin of the ARM mixer thread at 0x00517B6C: waits on svc 0x28 (svcGetSystemTick) for the DSP display event, runs the per-frame audio callbacks at +0x20/+0x28/+0x30 under the mixer mutex/monitor, calls Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate and loops while the run flag is set.
evidence: Named callees Sound_Frame_BeginUpdate, Os_MutexLock, Os_LockMonitor, Os_LockSemaphore and the svc 0x28 wait match the ARM twin's structure; the Thumb body is damaged (unaff_r4/r7) but the loop skeleton is readable.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectPassA
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectPassA(u32 flags, int scene, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Field2D scene render pass: dispatches the spatial grid, walks the 0xE0-byte object records issuing direct and quad draws for each live object, applies the per-object attributes and, when the render pipeline changed, runs the batch pass. Prologue lost (Thumb, unaff_r11).
evidence: Only the call set identifies it (Field2D_SpatialGrid_DispatchRenderObjectsB, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectsDirect/Quads, Field2D_Object_ApplyAttribute); the argument list is still a guess because the prologue was destroyed.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectPassB
summary: Second Field2D render pass (same object walk as 0x005C6E12 minus the flag byte): dispatches the spatial grid, issues direct/quad draws over the 0xE0-byte records, applies attributes and runs the batch pass plus the 0xE8-stride sprite list. Prologue lost.
evidence: Callees are a subset of 0x005C6E12's; unaff_r4/r5/r11 and in_stack_* show the damaged prologue, so the scene argument is inferred.

name: maybe_Party_IsReserveMember
summary: Returns 1 when the character's record has flag bit 0 clear and bit 1 set (read as 'not in the active party but still usable'), else 0. Reads CharacterRecord+4 resolved from the character id at member+0xC8.
evidence: 24 named callers, all menu/equipment roster enumerations (Ui_EquipWindow_LoadPreviewModel, Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshMemberIds, Shop_BuildFilteredItemList*, Menu_CreateEntryObjects); the two bits themselves are not documented anywhere in FACTS.

name: maybe_Battle_PickUnitNearAverageLevel
summary: Chooses a candidate unit from the work+0x2857C table whose level is within about +/-30% of the average party level; the action id in desc+0xC selects one of four weight tables that pick a sector (0..3), and the battle RNG picks the final entry.
evidence: Named callers Model_CreateActorModel and BattleScene_RefreshCommandWidgets plus the member-level average (func_0035EB98->f_D8) and the four weight tables are visible; the tolerance and sector arithmetic are read from constants (0.3, 4).

name: maybe_Item_CanBeUsedInContext
summary: Item acceptance test: when the item record is missing or its kind2 byte (+0x11) is not '#', it returns 1 unless the equipment model lookup fails; for '#' items (and the 0x9E0 whitelist) it instead requires one of two further lookups on the owner's sub-objects to succeed. The old 'CanUseItemOnSelf' claimed a target check the body does not perform.
evidence: Three named callers are all item/equipment panel refreshes (Ui_ItemPanel_RefreshFromConditions, Ui_EquipRow_Refresh, Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenItemPage) that pass a UI manager plus an item id; several callee names (Camera_UpdateOcclusionAndProjection) are clearly mis-resolved, so the exact rule is unclear.
